text:
mira: heads-up — I ran the new long-context synthetic suite (kv-reuse-frag) against nightly runtime and I'm seeing steady memory growth + fragmentation after ~200k tokens. repro steps below.

mira: minimal repro (local docker, n=1, looped prompts):
```
./bin/run_kv_bench --model gptx-small --seq 16384 --iterations 1000 --interleave 8 --enable-kv-paging
```

mira: sample tail of logs: 
```
[KV] slot_alloc: 2048 -> 3176 (frag: 22%)
[KV] paging: moved 1.2GB to disk cache (latency spike)
[mem] Resident: 8.1GB -> 10.5GB (+2.4GB) over 120k tokens
[perf] avg latency per token: 7.1ms -> 9.8ms after paging events
```

mira: PR 1427 touched eviction heuristics (LRU aging -> segment-based). CI perf showed flakiness. linking the run: https://ci.redwood/1745504321/kv-reuse-run (perf-bot added summary).

tony: interesting — can you share jemalloc stats and the exact paging backend (tmpfs vs disk)? frag numbers could be allocator-level.

mira: using tmpfs in docker. jemalloc stats (snapshot taken at 3 checkpoints):
```
--- jemalloc snapshot 1 ---
active: 7.9GB, dirty: 0.0GB, retained: 0.1GB
--- snapshot 3 (after growth) ---
active: 10.3GB, dirty: 0.0GB, retained: 0.3GB
```

alex: that looks like real active growth, not just fragmentation. Does the KV reuse logic evict properly when we page? If pages are moved out but slots remain allocated, the allocator still counts them. Could be leak in free path.

sam: can you run with KV debug logs enabled (KV_DEBUG=slot-ops, reuse) and attach? Also rerun with --reuse-threshold=0.5 to force earlier reuse.

mira: ran with reuse-threshold=0.5 — reduced resident growth by ~600MB but still grows slowly. debug dump shows many small freed segments remain in LRU but not reused because sizes mismatch (we're splitting 4K vs 6K segments).

julia: this matches a hypothesis: our segment allocator rounds to buckets, and we don't coalesce free adjacent slots after paging. That yields fragmentation over long sequences. In PR 1427 we changed eviction to favor older segments which might leave small holes.

tony: steps I propose:
- add deterministic synthetic test that interleaves allocations of varying KV lengths to reproduce bucket fragmentation
- add test that asserts resident growth delta < 200MB after 1M tokens
- instrument coalescing path and test enabling coalescing on free

mira: I'm already working on the deterministic test. Draft test scenario: allocate pattern A(8K) B(4K) A B A B ... then trigger paging, then request many new A-sized entries to force reallocation. If reuse fails, we'll see growth.

alex: also check kernel selection impact — some kernels materialize KV pages differently (sparse vs packed). Could be differences in mmap granularity. Maybe add a variant that disables sparse mmap to see oob.

perf-bot: perf comparison summary: baseline (master@1745400000) vs nightly (PR1427):
- memory peak: +18% (10.5GB vs 8.9GB)
- p50 token latency: +30%
- paging events: 4x more frequent
Link: https://perf.redwood/compare/1745400000...1745504321

mira: thanks — I've pushed a branch with the deterministic test and a small allocator coalesce change: branch kv/reuse-frag-1745504321. It lives at https://git.redwood/infra/kv/compare/kv/reuse-frag-1745504321. CI currently failing on a perf gate (expected).

tony: pinging @alex @sam for review. If coalescing fixes it we should add it behind a feature flag and add a targeted regression test that runs on the nightly perf suite (long-context).

sam: FYI I repro'd locally with the interleaved pattern and saw the same fragmentation. I tried enabling coalesce and resident stayed flat after 250k tokens. Patches look small; main risk is concurrency around free/coalesce (racy merges).

julia: let's also add an assertion in the long-context harness that checks total KV allocations don't monotonically increase for a fixed-key workload. That'll catch regressions earlier.

mira: agreed. I'll:
- add the deterministic interleave test to unit/perf/kv_long_reuse_test
- gate coalesce behind env var REDWOOD_KV_COALESCE=1
- add the harness assertion for non-monotonic kv_alloc_count

alex: one more ask: add a micro-benchmark of slot-size distribution (histogram) to the perf artifacts. That makes it easy to spot bucket skew.

mira: will do. I'll leave the branch open, add logs and a small run artifact in CI. If reviewers +1, we can merge behind flag and enable on nightly week rollout.

ci-bot: build #4821 for branch kv/reuse-frag-1745504321 finished: tests=passed, perf-gate=failed (memory growth). See https://ci.redwood/4821

tony: thanks all. Priorities: reproduce reliably (done), add regression test (mira), ensure concurrency safety for coalesce (sam), add histograms to perf artifacts (alex). After that we can flip flag on nightly and monitor.

mira: tagging this thread for follow-up in next eng-runtime sync. I'll post a short runbook once we merge. :thumbsup:

alex: +1. good catch.

sam: reviewing now.

julia: thanks, will watch the perf dashboard. :eyes:

mira: attaching the short run log to the ticket — will update when CI passes.
